description: Total curvature as the computable half of the serpenoid tower. Milnor: inf over the isotopy class of the total curvature equals 2*pi*b(L), and b(L) >= mu + #knotted components. The canonical closure has mu = A+1 components (exact integer permutation cycle count, probe-derived at A=2,3,4,6; carried as hypothesis hmu : mu = A+1 in SLq2LabelParity.lean:77 and TorusKnotPages.lean:82, bean qou-d5hn) of which A are (2,odd)-torus knots on both classical branches (exact-integer Kauffman bracket), so inf total curvature >= 2*pi*(2A+1): extensive with slope 4*pi per nucleon. Under Crofton, curvature = pi * (mean number of critical points of the height functions), which is the precise form of 'the oscillations happen at the saddle points'. The twist is not produced here.
caveats: The canonical word is a Hecke element, not a braid: its 2A+1 averaged letters have no crossing sign. Everything geometric here is per classical branch. A link-theoretic statement about the un-resolved object does not exist, and this probe does not make one.

Knot types are read from the Jones polynomial. Jones distinguishes the (2,odd)-torus knots from the unknot unconditionally (non-trivial polynomial => knotted); naming a component T(2,k) from its Jones polynomial alone is an identification, safe at these crossing numbers.

The lower bound 2*pi*(2A+1) is a theorem about every geometric realisation of the closure. It is NOT a substrate observable and it is NOT connected to binding by anything here. Its extensivity is noted because the theta_lambda gate needed an extensive channel; that is an observation about shape, not a mechanism.
This is the curvature half. The hull-exit analysis puts the missing ingredient in the twist, a torsion integral the osculating circle is blind to. Nothing here supplies it.
